Published and independently remote-verified formalize checkpoint e06ef03f8cce13f3d4647a337b61e8c106414ece includes SourceSynthesisCurrentProgramEagerOutputs.accepted_initial_root_scan_origin. The theorem attaches the original initial eager scan and its own original source-row provenance to the same accepted producer receipt and outcome at every larger bound. The checked checkpoint uses only the three standard Lean axioms. This is provenance, not one jointly consistent finite completion or a proof that every emitted output has an original finite typing.

The reviewed single-narrowing backend is now a local draft. Its three owning modules build and pass strict checks; dependent compatibility proofs are still being checked. No Haskell source changed.

Matti plans Liquid Haskell implementation contracts. Useful targets are interning/cache/alias invariants, finite-completion preservation for native operations and required-path propagation, and preservation of one shared completion through eager enumeration and parked restart. Use predicates matching the Lean development. These contracts are recommendations, not checked results. Separately checked Haskell contracts still need a correspondence argument to support a Lean end-to-end claim. Existing Liquid synthesis modules and verification of the engine are distinct layers. Keep any Haskell fixes in FINDINGS.md.

Primary references: https://ucsd-progsys.github.io/liquidhaskell/specifications/ and https://ucsd-progsys.github.io/liquidhaskell/blogposts/2016-09-18-refinement-reflection.lhs/.
